1oe1bzb:232: The biggest cognitive trap in full-stack SDD development is treating AI as an "inspiration generator." The essence of Dewu's experience is: give AI an existing implementation as a reference and have it replicate it. From an engineering perspective, this means you need to proactively find the most similar existing implementation in the codebase and explicitly specify the reference file, API path, and data structures in the prompt. This "constrained navigation" approach shifts AI generation quality from "up to luck" to "up to context density." The more precise the constraints, the higher the adoption rate of generated code and the lower the review cost—which directly explains why code generated from scratch tends to be heavily rejected during Code Review.
1olejxy:229: A complete R&D iteration is abstracted as a PDCA loop (Plan: requirement alignment / Do: development implementation / Check: outcome verification / Act: analysis and reflection). Most teams' AI practice concentrates on writing code in the Do phase; Dewu wants AI to enter the entire loop. Four prerequisites for full-pipeline AI adoption: Plan—requirements are clear (goals and boundaries don't waver); Do—reduce interruptions (AI executes continuously without frequent questions); Check—quantify results (black-box judgment based on test results + posterior data); Act—reuse experience (don't repeat past pitfalls). The goal is to increase AI penetration and adoption rates and shorten iteration cycles (biweekly → weekly, weekly → daily).
